Subject: PrivDeploy entry criteria + ops contact matrix — MedSync kickoff

Team —

MedSync (external) asked for a quick kickoff next week to start private deployment intake. I put together a concise "entry criteria" workbook and an ops contact matrix (attached) so we have a clean checklist to share with the customer during the call. Can you review the checklist and confirm owners for the network preflight and day-0 engineer? High level asks from MedSync:

- VPC peering / private interconnect (they may bring a circuit)
- KMS & key rotation pattern (customer-managed keys preferred)
- Audit log retention and S3 access patterns
- Smoke test plan (sample traffic + telemetry checks)

Attachments: privdeploy-entry-criteria.xlsx, ops-contact-matrix.csv

Proposed kickoff: Tue 2025-10-07 10:00 AM PDT (I suggested). If that works, I will invite MedSync and send the latest checklist as our shared intake doc.

Quick asks:
- Ben — can you scope the day0 engineer and own the smoke test plan?
- Kimberly — can you verify the network rules section (IP ranges/egress ports) and add anything we should pre-request from MedSync?

Thanks — Sean

--
Sean Gallagher

On Sun, Oct 5, 2025 at 11:04 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sean — thanks for the draft. I ran through the checklist and added a Day-0 roles PDF (attached) with recommended owners:

Thanks — added a few concrete network asks to the checklist:

Network preflight (to request from MedSync before day-0):
- Customer public IPs for peering (if they are terminating a circuit) and expected source IP ranges from their side
- ASN and BGP neighbors (if using BGP)
- Allowed egress ports from Redwood to customer endpoints: 443 (TLS), 123 (NTP) for time sync if they require it, 22 only for bastion-originated troubleshooting (minimize)
- MTU target (we've seen issues when circuits force 9000 vs 1500) — add test for jumbo frames
- NAT and SNAT expectations for egressed telemetry (we prefer private ranges but want to confirm)

Firewall sample (informational):
- Allow outbound 443 to customer IP ranges
- Allow inbound TCP 1024-65535 for ephemeral return (stateful expected)

I'll also prepare a brief runbook snippet for Day-0 peering validation and attach to the Drive folder. Please call out anything we need to escalate to infra before the customer call.

Kimberly
Network Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Marie Fischer <marie.fischer@medsync.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2025 09:27:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy entry criteria + ops contact matrix — MedSync kickoff

Hi Sean / team —

Thanks for pulling this together. Tue 10/7 10:00 AM PDT works for our network and infra leads — I'll invite: ops@medsync.com (network lead: Tomas Alvarez). A few notes from our side so you have them ahead of the call:

- We'll provide public IPs + ASN by EOD today.
- We plan to bring a single 10Gb circuit for private connectivity; we'll confirm MTU and whether jumbo frames are enabled on the circuit.
- SOC2 excerpt (control description for logging/retention) will be attached to the kickoff invite as a PDF.
- We prefer customer-managed KMS keys and will provide the principal for cross-account key access.

On smoke tests: we want to run a simple end-to-end inference test (one-shot text generation) and a 5-minute ramp to 20 RPS to validate capacity and token accounting. If you have a standby Day-0 engineer, that will be helpful.

Marie
VP, IT Operations | MedSync Health
marie.fischer@medsync.com
